reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address the key premises. E1 discusses binary/ternary Mg-Zn-Ti alloys and their corrosion, not metastable microstructures or phase evolution in HEAs. E2 mentions solid-solution and intermetallic phases in as-cast and heat-treated lightweight CCAs but provides no data on metastability, diffusion-driven evolution, or its effects on oxidation and corrosion. The premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: As-cast Mg-containing lightweight HEAs contain a metastable supersaturated solid-solution matrix with fine non-equilibrium intermetallic particles
Thermal exposure causes diffusion-driven evolution of these metastable phases into stable intermetallic compounds
This phase evolution modifies local chemistry at phase boundaries
The modified chemistry promotes formation of uniform, protective oxide scales (MgO, Al2O3) during high-temperature oxidation
The evolution reduces micro-galvanic corrosion sites, altering corrosion behavior
